title: Finite products and the zero abelian variety
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $J$ be a finite set, and let $A_j/k$ for $j\in J$ be abelian varieties [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Their scheme product $P=\prod_{j\in J}A_j$ over $k$, with componentwise group operations [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product], is an abelian variety and $\dim P=\sum_{j\in J}\dim A_j$. For $J=\varnothing$ the product is the trivial group scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Conversely every zero-dimensional abelian variety over $k$ is isomorphic, as a $k$-group scheme, to $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, lemma-dimension-product-locally-algebraic; Groupoid Schemes Tags 03RO (definition-abelian-variety), 0B7Q (lemma-connected-group-scheme-over-field-irreducible), 0BFC (lemma-abelian-variety-smooth). Products use stability of properness and smoothness and geometric connectedness; the zero-dimensional case is smooth and geometrically integral with a rational identity.

proof.text: The empty product in $k$-schemes is $\operatorname{Spec}k$: a test $k$-scheme has exactly one morphism to it, its structure map. Its multiplication, inverse and unit are the unique possible $k$-maps, so all group diagrams commute. Its structure morphism is the identity, which is proper and smooth directly from their definitions, and its underlying space is a singleton. It is therefore an abelian variety by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Its only local ring is $k$, whose only prime ideal is $(0)$, so its dimension is $0$ [def-pc-dimension]. This is also the empty sum.

source.place: Tag 03RO, definition-abelian-variety; empty product and identity morphism checked from the definitions

proof.text: For two factors $A,B$, form $P=A\times_kB$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $m_P$ by its two components $m_A\circ(p_A,p_A)$ and $m_B\circ(p_B,p_B)$, where each pair uses the corresponding projections from the two copies of $P$; define $i_P=(i_Ap_A,i_Bp_B)$ and $e_P=(e_A,e_B)$. Each group diagram becomes the corresponding diagram in $A$ or $B$ after either projection and hence commutes by uniqueness in the fibre-product property [def-sc-group-scheme]. The projection $P\to B$ is the base change of $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so it is proper and smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Composing with $B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] and smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition].

source.place: Tags 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper), 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper), 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); product group construction from Groupoid Schemes Tag 022S (definition-group-scheme).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $A$ is geometrically integral. By [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme], every field extension of $A$ is nonempty and irreducible, hence connected, so $A$ is geometrically connected. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] with $X=A,Y=B$. Since $B$ is nonempty and connected, it has one connected component; therefore $P$ has exactly one nonempty connected component and is connected. Together with the preceding step, the definition [def-sc-abelian-variety] makes $P$ an abelian variety.

source.place: Tag 0B7Q, lemma-connected-group-scheme-over-field-irreducible; Tag 03RO; Varieties connected-component projection argument; Varieties Tag 0385 (lemma-bijection-connected-components).

proof.text: Induct on the cardinality of the finite set $J$. The base case is step 1. For $J=I\amalg\{j\}$, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the $J$-product, with its coordinate group operations, with $(\prod_{i\in I}A_i)\times_kA_j$. The induction hypothesis and steps 2–3 make it an abelian variety. Both factors are nonempty and finite type, since abelian varieties are connected and proper. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-product-dimension] to obtain $\dim P=\dim(\prod_{i\in I}A_i)+\dim A_j=\sum_{i\in I}\dim A_i+\dim A_j$. Thus the induction establishes both the abelian-variety assertion and the stated dimension equality for every finite $J$.

Now let $A/k$ be an abelian variety with $\dim A=0$. Properness includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite] makes $A$ affine. It is geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] to the proper geometrically integral $k$-scheme $A$: the structural map $k\to\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$ is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. Since both $A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are affine, [lem-sc-affine-global-sections-iso] makes the structure map $f:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ an isomorphism of $k$-schemes.

source.place: Tag 06LH, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0; Tag 0BUG, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections, clause (8); Tag 04L2, lemma-regular-functions-proper-variety, clause (4)

proof.text: The map $f$ of step 5 is a homomorphism to the trivial group scheme: its multiplication-compatibility diagram consists of two $k$-maps $A\times_k A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which are equal by uniqueness of the structure map. Its inverse is the identity section $e_A$, since $f e_A=1$ and $f$ is invertible. To check that this inverse is a homomorphism, compose $m_A(e_A\times e_A)$ and $e_A m_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$ with the isomorphism $f$; both composites are the unique $k$-map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so cancellation gives equality. Thus $f$ is an isomorphism as $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], as required.
